answer.says: Ramesh, I will not keep you standing. You have made the tea, which is the only thing that has been made today. Sit down. I will take a walk to the gardens; the air is hazy, but the domes are still there, and I need to see something that was built by a will other than my own. I will be back before the dark sets in completely.
answer.thought: The tea is strong, as requested, and it tastes of the dust that clings to the leaves. Ramesh stands by the stove, his face a mask of patient endurance, the bondsman who knows his lord is merely a confused guest. I must leave this room; the walls are closing in with the weight of my own inability to act, and the need for movement is the only dialectic I can still resolve.
